title: Finite coefficient change for ordinary direct image
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$
and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra finite as an $A$-module, with
its constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let
$T,X$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:T\to X$ be separated of
finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $K$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-module sheaves on the small étale site
of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], with finite Tor amplitude:
there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L M)=0$
for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ in degree zero and $i\notin[a,b]$
(the étale convention in [lem-sf-flat-model]). Write $K_B=K\otimes_A^L B$
for ordinary uncompleted étale derived extension of scalars, viewed in
$D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], whose underlying
$A$-complex is the derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then the
canonical coefficient projection map
$$
c_{f,K}^{A\to B}:(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^L B
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,B}(K_B)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. It is defined by the
$B$-coefficient inverse-image/direct-image adjunction: its transpose is
the $B$-extension of the $A$-coefficient counit, after the canonical
pullback/scalar-extension identification
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Upon restriction
to $A$-coefficients [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], it is the projection
map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] followed by the canonical
restriction/direct-image comparison
[lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Use derived
étale direct images as in
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. It is natural in $K$. For separated
finite-type maps $T\xrightarrow{f}X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ of finite-type
$k$-schemes, the equality
$$
c_{gf,K}^{A\to B}
=Rg_{*,B}(c_{f,K}^{A\to B})\circ c_{g,Rf_{*,A}K}^{A\to B}
$$
holds after the canonical direct-image composition identifications
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. For a commutative $B$-algebra
$C$ finite as a $B$-module, with coefficient chain $A\to B\to C$, the equality
$$
c_{f,K}^{A\to C}
=c_{f,K_B}^{B\to C}\circ(c_{f,K}^{A\to B}\otimes_B^L C)
$$
holds after tensor reassociation; $c_{f,K_B}^{B\to C}$ denotes the
same counit construction over $B$, whether or not $B$ is itself a ring
$A_{E,m}$. Let $\nu_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to
W_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]
for each scheme $W$, and put $K_{\mathrm{pro}}=\nu_T^*K$ and
$K_{\mathrm{pro},B}=\nu_T^*K_B$, with exact derived comparison pullback
[def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. The canonical pro-étale map
$$
(Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,A}K_{\mathrm{pro}})\otimes_A^L B
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,B}(K_{\mathrm{pro},B})
$$
is also an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and satisfies the
same naturality and coherence identities. Here the map is defined by
the analogous $B$-coefficient adjunction transpose, with pro-étale
direct images of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]
and pro-étale derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor].

proof.text: Identify the existing uniquely specified coefficient map with the geometric mate of the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of the exact restriction/pullback square. The scalar-unit identity and the two adjunction bijections prove the identification and naturality; no faithfulness of derived restriction is used.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 1

proof.text: For geometric composition, paste the exact restriction/pullback squares and take inverse mates. The canonical right-derived direct-image compositor is the conjugate of the canonical left-derived pullback compositor. Apply the generic exchange-composition identity. For a coefficient chain, use the unit of the composite scalar adjunction, the restriction compositor, its mate defining the scalar compositor, and uniqueness of left adjoints. These computations apply on both sites, for arbitrary commutative rings and complexes.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 2

proof.text: A finite coefficient ring A is Noetherian, and a finite A-algebra B is finitely presented as an A-module. The finite-type source has a finite Krull-dimension bound. Over the separably closed base field, the published uniform all-sheaf direct-image bound applies. Use the proved intermediate projection component in the existing finite-constant projection theorem, before its canonical constant-pullback identifications. Exact constant/restriction commutation identifies the constant A-module B with the scalar coefficient sheaf, so naturality transfers invertibility to the required projection component.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 3

proof.text: Identify the two specified forward scalar/pullback isomorphisms. The ordinary reverse mate is the inverse ordinary scalar/pullback isomorphism, by iterated mates and the restriction/direct-image adjunction identity. On cochains its scalar-unit equation holds componentwise. The exact derived geometric representatives commute with the localized restriction square. Applying the derived scalar adjunction to this square gives the normalization of the reverse mate; invert it and invoke uniqueness of the normalized forward isomorphism. This verifies compatibility of the actual canonical maps, rather than replacing either by an arbitrary isomorphism. The compatibility module now reuses the normalized canonical definition and supplies its proved inverse-mate identification as a private definition API; the item uses the common definition.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 4

proof.text: Finite Tor amplitude gives a lower bound for scalar extension of K, using the scalar/tensor comparison and faithful exact restriction on cohomology. The projection isomorphism and left t-exactness of derived direct image give a lower bound for the scalar extension of Rf_*K by the same reflection argument. Thus all three objects in the recorded projection/mate identity admit bounded-below representatives; no direct-image Tor-amplitude or output constructibility theorem is needed. Compute the ambient restriction/direct-image mate on D+ using the published derived adjunction unit and counit identities. It is the canonical bounded-below restriction comparison and is invertible. The projection/mate identity then shows that restriction of the coefficient mate is invertible. Faithful exact restriction detects zero cohomology and reflects isomorphisms.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 5

proof.text: Specialize the preceding generic finite-ring argument to the lifted positive-level coefficient ring. Its finiteness is the published coefficient-extension theorem, and the geometric base is algebraically closed, hence separably closed. Bounded constructibility supplies upper and lower cohomological bounds, and the given Tor-amplitude interval supplies the scalar-extension lower bound. This proves the unchanged etale isomorphism statement.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 6

proof.text: For etale-origin pro-etale inputs, apply the recorded canonical etale/pro-etale scalar-mate compatibility square. The etale map is invertible by the preceding step. The canonical scalar/comparison and direct-image comparison maps in the square are invertible on the bounded-below input and its bounded-below scalar extension. Cancel these isomorphisms to obtain invertibility of the specified pro-etale map. Naturality and both coherence identities have already been proved without boundedness in Step 2.

source.place: Finite coefficient direct image; implementation step 7
